edits.content:
## Exact Option Comparison
- For a “strongest valid claim” question, compare options across separate dimensions: existence versus uniqueness, local versus global solvability, endpoint inclusion, global versus local regularity, and any additional hypotheses. Select the strongest claim supported on every dimension.
- Audit quantifiers and logical connectors literally. An “if” statement is not an “if and only if”; a universal claim is not an existential one; and removing a hypothesis makes a genuinely stronger claim that needs separate justification. Check limit conditions such as limsup and liminf exactly as written.
- When choices are small variations of a theorem-like claim, verify the exact assumptions and quantitative threshold rather than relying on a remembered or approximate version. Do not infer that a stronger bound or broader conclusion follows merely because a weaker one does.
- If options differ only by a sign, factor, logarithm base, exponent, or inequality direction, check the expression directly—using algebra, an admissible special case, or an exact comparison—instead of choosing by pattern or intuition.
